analysis.summary: Brazil, five-time world champions and tournament favorites, open Group C against a Morocco side that reached the Qatar 2022 semifinal and won all eight of their World Cup qualifying matches. Brazil enter with notable absences — Rodrygo (torn ACL/meniscus, out for 2026), Militao (hamstring surgery), and Estevao (hamstring) — while Neymar is listed as game-time doubtful with a calf complaint. Morocco are without Ziyech, En-Nesyri, and Abde Ezzalzouli (injury), but Hakimi recovered from his thigh issue in time to play. The market strongly favors Brazil, but Morocco's defensive organization — they conceded zero in four consecutive wins heading into the tournament — means this opener carries genuine upset potential.
analysis.home_form: Brazil won 3-1 vs Croatia (friendly, March 2026), lost 1-2 to France (friendly, March 2026), drew 1-1 with Tunisia (friendly, November 2025), won 2-0 vs Senegal (friendly, November 2025), and lost 2-3 to Japan (Kirin Cup, October 2025). Mixed form overall: 2W/1D/2L in last 5, scoring 9 and conceding 7. Carlo Ancelotti took over in May 2025 and has been developing the system, but key absentees (Rodrygo, Militao, Estevao, doubtful Neymar) deplete the squad's depth significantly.
analysis.away_form: Morocco qualified with a perfect record (8W from 8) for the World Cup and entered on strong form: 3-0 vs Zambia (Dec 2025), 1-0 vs Tanzania (Jan 2026), 2-0 vs Cameroon (Jan 2026), 0-0 draw vs Nigeria (Jan 2026), and 3-0 vs Senegal (Jan 2026) — these last matches during AFCON 2026. Four wins and one draw, conceding zero goals in the last four matches. They were also the first African semi-finalists in World Cup history at Qatar 2022, dispatching Spain and Portugal along the way.
analysis.h2h: Three all-time meetings: Brazil won 2-0 (friendly, 1997), Brazil won 3-0 at France 1998 World Cup, Morocco won 2-1 (friendly, March 2023). Brazil lead 2-1 on wins. The most recent meeting in 2023 saw Morocco claim their first-ever win over Brazil, underlining the competitive shift in African football.
injuries_news: Rodrygo (Brazil): torn ACL and outer meniscus, out for remainder of 2026 — confirmed absence
Militao (Brazil): hamstring surgery, out for World Cup — confirmed absence
Estevao (Brazil): hamstring injury, left off Brazil's squad — confirmed absence
Neymar (Brazil): calf injury, listed as game-time doubtful; Igor Thiago expected to start if Neymar misses
Hakim Ziyech (Morocco): not selected for the 2026 World Cup squad
Youssef En-Nesyri (Morocco): not selected for the 2026 World Cup squad
Abde Ezzalzouli (Morocco): injury doubt, World Cup participation under threat
Noussair Mazraoui (Morocco): shoulder injury, expected to start
Achraf Hakimi (Morocco): thigh injury during Champions League semi-final, recovered and played 65 minutes vs Norway pre-tournament
key_factors: Brazil's attacking depth is thinned significantly without Rodrygo, Militao, Estevao, and potentially Neymar; Vinicius Junior and Raphinha remain elite threats
Morocco's defensive organization under Regragui has been exceptional — conceded 0 in 4 consecutive wins; historically held Spain, Portugal, and Belgium to 0 at Qatar 2022
Morocco beat Brazil 2-1 in March 2023, demonstrating they are no longer purely reactive and can expose gaps on the counter
MetLife Stadium in June will see temperatures of approximately 27°C+ with high humidity; FIFA has mandated cooling breaks for all matches regardless of temperature, partly neutralizing this factor
MetLife Stadium is near sea level (~50 ft), so no altitude disadvantage for either side
Brazil's probable lineup: Alisson; Wesley, Marquinhos, Gabriel, Alex Sandro; Casemiro, Bruno Guimaraes; Raphinha, Lucas Paqueta, Vinicius Junior; Matheus Cunha (or Igor Thiago if Neymar is fully out)
Morocco's probable lineup: Bounou; Hakimi, Diop, Riad, Mazraoui; El Aynaoui, Bouaddi, Ounahi; Brahim Diaz, El Kaabi, Saibari

This is both teams' Group C opener — maximum motivation; Brazil need to establish authority to manage the group; Morocco need points against the strongest opponent first to give themselves breathing room
